command: Human BCL2 can positively regulate apoptotic processes after caspase cleavage or conformational conversion, and can form functional channels or pores contributing to transmembrane transport. Evaluate these claims independently against full primary studies including PMID:9395403, PMID:14980220 and PMID:9219694, target construct/processing state, assay pH and membrane context. Distinguish predominant native antiapoptotic function from demonstrated conditional intrinsic capacities. Establish which gene product performs the proapoptotic step and whether transport evidence reflects intrinsic BCL2 pore formation or regulation of another channel. Read actual PAINT node placement, descendant evidence and loss/divergence; do not use family-role exclusivity or absent target assays alone to reject ancestral assertions. Consider whether conclusions extend to mouse Bcl2 with species-specific primary support.
